title: strand-aware KV slot allocator and decoder scheduling with prefill-priority fencing
creator: Maya Gupta
description: Introduce a strand-aware KV slot allocator and decoder scheduling policy that separates long-lived conversational strands from transient requests to reduce fragmentation and prefill-induced decode stalls. The allocator will maintain soft isolation windows (fences) for high-priority strands so their KV footprints are preserved across prefill waves, while low-priority or cold strands are compacted eagerly. Decoder scheduling uses strand hints to prefer warm-KV placements and to gate prefill throughput when contention threatens tail latency.
background: Recent customer workloads exhibit high fragmentation in the paged KV cache where short-lived assistant tasks interleave with long-running chat strands. This causes repeated prefill/eviction churn and intermittent decode stalls when large prefill waves evict active strand pages. Existing strategies (LRU windows, soft quotas) reduce average eviction but do not account for conversational locality or relative strand priority. We experimented with coalescing fragments and temporal anchors but need a scheduling-aware allocator that interacts with kernel selection and prefill pacing.
tasks: Instrument trace collector to emit strand_id and active_prefix_length for requests (backend + runtime hooks).
Design allocator data structures: per-shard strand table, soft-fence epoch counters, and compactability score per slot.
Implement allocator prototype: strand-based slot tagging, gentle-fencing logic and background consolidator.
Add decoder scheduler: strand-priority queue, warm-KV placement heuristic and prefill backpressure signals.
Expose kernel-hint API so allocator/scheduler can mark blocks as fast-path (packed) or slow-path (staged).
Create offline simulator using production traces to validate hit-rate, prefill volume, and stall frequency.
Integrate metrics: p95/p99 decode latency, prefill_bytes_per_minute, cache_fragmentation_ratio, strand_eviction_rate.
E2E tests: synthetic mixed-workload (chat + short completions) and smoke on Dedicated cluster.
Prepare rollout plan: canary on 5% traffic, monitor regressions, progressive ramp to 100% with rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=12% reduction in prefill traffic for active strands on representative traces.
Production canary (5%) shows no regression in p99 tail decode latency and reduces strand_eviction_rate by >=20% within 24h.
No increased token-cost beyond 5% for mixed workloads; telemetry for cost impact is available in console route dashboard.
Kernel-hint path correctly routes fast-path allocations to optimized kernels in at least two model families in the catalog.
Documentation for allocator knobs and scheduler flags added to internal runbook and public console KB.
decisions: Use strand_id derived from conversation_id + user_session as primary affinity key (rather than request hash) to improve locality stability.
Fencing is soft: epochs decrease over time and are revocable under memory pressure to avoid starvation.
Allocator will operate per-KV-shard to avoid global locks; global consolidation runs only in off-peak windows.
Decoder scheduler uses a token-bucket style backpressure signal from allocator when prefill volume crosses a shard threshold.
